G4672.d: Solomon (i.e. Shelomoh), the son of David
fb: King living at the time of United Monarchy
David and Bathsheba's son, and Israel's third king. He was rushed onto the throne after his half-brother Adonijah tried to take it while David lay dying. Early on he asked God for wisdom.

G4639.d: "shade" or a shadow (literally or figuratively (darkness of error or an adumbration))

G4613.d: Simon (i.e. Shimon), the name of nine Israelites
fb: Man living at the time of the New Testament
Simon Peter, called from his fishing in Matthew 4:18 and named first among the twelve apostles. In Matthew 16:16 he is the one who answers the question.
Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
One of the twelve apostles. The title Zealot tells him apart from Simon Peter and probably means he had belonged to a movement opposed to Roman rule. Nothing else about him is recorded.
Man living at the time of the New Testament
A tanner whose house was by the sea. Peter lodged with him, and the messengers in Acts 10:17 came to his gate asking for Peter.
Man living at the time of the New Testament
He practised magic and had the people amazed, until he believed and was baptized himself. Then he offered the apostles money for their power, and Peter told him his money could perish with him.
Man living at the time of the New Testament
John names him three times, and every time as the father of the disciple who handed his master over.
Man living at the time of the New Testament
The man made to carry the cross on the way to the crucifixion, in Matthew 27:32, Mark 15:21 and Luke 23:26.
Man living at the time of the New Testament
One of 7 men called Simon. This one is a man from the New Testament, named twice in Matthew and Mark.

G4624.d: to entrap, i.e. trip up (figuratively, stumble (transitively) or entice to sin, apostasy or displeasure)

G4600.d: the jaw-bone, i.e. (by implication) the cheek or side of the face

G4659.d: angry-visaged, i.e. gloomy or affecting a mournful appearance

G4687.d: to scatter, i.e. sow (literally or figuratively)

G4697.d: to have the bowels yearn, i.e. (figuratively) feel sympathy, to pity

G4670.d: Sodoma (i.e. Sedom), a place in Palestine
fb: Sodom was destroyed by fire from heaven along with Gomorrah, and the rest of Scripture keeps pointing back to it as the picture of judgment. It was one of the cities of the plain near the Dead Sea.

G4678.d: wisdom (higher or lower, worldly or spiritual)

G4605.d: Sidon (i.e. Tsidon), a place in Palestine
fb: The older of the two great Phoenician ports, north of Tyre. It was allotted to Asher, but Asher never took it.
Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
Genesis and 1 Chronicles name him twice, and he is a man from the patriarchs.

G4632.d: a vessel, implement, equipment or apparatus (literally or figuratively [specially, a wife as contributing to the usefulness of the husband])

G4650.d: to dissipate, i.e. (figuratively) put to flight, waste, be liberal

G4690.d: something sown, i.e. seed (including the male "sperm"); by implication, offspring; specially, a remnant (figuratively, as if kept over for planting)

G4625.d: a trap-stick (bent sapling), i.e. snare (figuratively, cause of displeasure or sin)

G4633.d: a tent or cloth hut (literally or figuratively)

G4623.d: properly, muteness, i.e. involuntary stillness, or inability to speak; and thus differing from G4602 (σιγή), which is rather a voluntary refusal or indisposition to speak, although the terms are often used synonymously); to be dumb (but not deaf also, like 2974 properly); figuratively, to be calm (as quiet water)

G4622.d: Sion (i.e. Tsijon), a hill of Jerusalem; figuratively, the Church (militant or triumphant)
fb: Another spelling of Zion. The hill in Jerusalem came to stand for the whole city, and in poetry for the place where God lives among his people.
Named once, in Deuteronomy, and nowhere else.

G4693.d: a cavern; by implication, a hiding-place or resort

G4642.d: dry, i.e. hard or tough (figuratively, harsh, severe)

G4686.d: a coil (spira, "spire"), i.e. (figuratively) a mass of men (a Roman military cohort; also (by analogy) a squad of Levitical janitors)

G4616.d: byssos, i.e. bleached linen (the cloth or a garment of it)

G4682.d: apparently strengthened from G4685 (σπάω) through the idea of spasmodic contraction); to mangle, i.e. convluse with epilepsy

G4688.d: a speculator, i.e. military scout (spy or (by extension) life-guardsman)

G4669.d: to tincture with myrrh, i.e. embitter (as a narcotic)

G4608.d: an intoxicant, i.e. intensely fermented liquor

G4640.d: to jump, i.e. sympathetically move (as the quickening of a fetus)

G4698.d: an intestine (plural); figuratively, pity or sympathy

G4683.d: from a derivative of the base of G4682 (σπαράσσω) meaning to strap or wrap with strips); to swathe (an infant after the Oriental custom)

G4692.d: to "speed" ("study"), i.e. urge on (diligently or earnestly); by implication, to await eagerly

G4606.d: a Sidonian, i.e. inhabitant of Sidon

G4673.d: a funereal receptacle (urn, coffin), i.e. (by analogy) a bier

fb: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
She traveled with Jesus and the twelve and paid toward their keep out of her own means, named in Luke 8:3 next to Mary Magdalene and Joanna. Nothing more is recorded about her.

G4661.d: something stripped (as a hide), i.e. booty

G4648.d: to take aim at (spy), i.e. (figuratively) regard

G4620.d: a grain-measure, i.e. (by implication) ration (allowance of food)

G4611.d: Siloam (i.e. Shiloach), a pool of Jerusalem
fb: The pool of Siloam in Jerusalem was fed by Hezekiah's tunnel. Jesus put mud on the eyes of a man born blind and sent him to wash there, and he came back seeing. Archaeologists have uncovered the pool's stone steps.

G4676.d: a sudarium (sweat-cloth), i.e. towel (for wiping the perspiration from the face, or binding the face of a corpse)

fb: Man living at the time of the New Testament
The Latin form of Silas. Paul uses it in his letters, and so does 1 Peter.

G4637.d: to tent or encamp, i.e. (figuratively) to occupy (as a mansion) or (specially), to reside (as God did in the Tabernacle of old, a symbol of protection and communion)

G4634.d: the Festival of Tabernacles (so called from the custom of erecting booths for temporary homes)

G4628.d: through the idea of leanness); the leg (as lank)

G4614.d: Sina (i.e. Sinai), a mountain in Arabia
fb: Sinai, in its Greek form. Stephen uses it when he tells of God appearing to Moses at the mountain. Paul turns Mount Sinai into an allegory in Galatians.

G4638.d: an encampment, i.e. (figuratively) the Temple (as God's residence), the body (as a tenement for the soul)

fb: Man living at the time of the New Testament
A leader in the Jerusalem church who went with Paul on his second missionary journey, after Paul and Barnabas split up. He is probably the Silvanus of Paul's letters.

G4691.d: a seed-picker (as the crow), i.e. (figuratively) a sponger, loafer (specially, a gossip or trifler in talk)

G4612.d: a semicinctium or half-girding, i.e. narrow covering (apron)

fb: Priest living at the time of the New Testament
Acts calls him a chief priest. No high priest of that name appears in the records, so it probably means he stood high among the Jews of Ephesus.

G4607.d: a dagger-man or assassin; a freebooter (Jewish fanatic outlawed by the Romans)

G4627.d: a "skiff" (as if dug out), or yawl (carried aboard a large vessel for landing)

fb: Paul meant to go on to Spain from Rome, once he had taken the collection to the poor in Jerusalem, and he hoped the Roman church would help him on his way. Whether he ever got there is not known.

G4636.d: a hut or temporary residence, i.e. (figuratively) the human body (as the abode of the spirit)

G4647.d: withered at the front, i.e. a point or prickle (figuratively, a bodily annoyance or disability)

G4656.d: to obscure or blind (literally or figuratively)

G4696.d: a stain or blemish, i.e. (figuratively) defect, disgrace

G4689.d: to pour out as a libation, i.e. (figuratively) to devote (one's life or blood, as a sacrifice) ("spend")

G4657.d: what is thrown to the dogs, i.e. refuse (ordure)

G4649.d: perhaps akin to G4626 (σκάπτω) through the idea of concealment; compare G4629 (σκέπασμα)); a watch (sentry or scout), i.e. (by implication) a goal

G4658.d: a Scythene or Scythian, i.e. (by implication) a savage
fb: Not a name but a people: nomads from the steppes north of the Black Sea and Caspian Sea, and the ancient byword for distant outsiders. Paul puts the Scythian in his list in Colossians 3:11.

G4629.d: perhaps akin to the base of G4649 (σκοπός) through the idea of noticeableness); clothing

G4679.d: to render wise; in a sinister acceptation, to form "sophisms", i.e. continue plausible error

G4695.d: to stain or soil (literally or figuratively)

G4694.d: a ledge or reef of rock in the sea

G4667.d: Smyrna, a place in Asia Minor
fb: About forty miles north of Ephesus, on the coast of Asia Minor. The church at Smyrna was one of the seven in Revelation, and it got no rebuke, only a warning that suffering was coming.

G4665.d: the emerald or green gem so called
